body:
## Pull request overview

This PR enhances the dashboard table/pivot widget experience by adding async object-provider support for table/pivot widgets, making the widget configuration panel type-aware, and addressing several dashboard UX issues (overflow handling, empty states, label rendering).

**Changes:**
- Added `ObjectDataTable` and `ObjectPivotTable` async wrappers and registered them as `object-data-table` / `object-pivot`; updated `DashboardRenderer` routing to use them for object-bound widgets.
- Made `WidgetConfigPanel` context-aware via `visibleWhen` sections, added pivot widget type option, and improved I18nLabel rendering behavior.
- Improved dashboard UX: grid span clamping, metric card truncation/overflow fixes, pivot table friendly empty state and totals styling; updated tests and ROADMAP.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 14 out of 14 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/types/src/designer.ts | Adds `pivot` to supported dashboard widget types. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx | Exports/registers new object-aware table/pivot components in the registry. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/WidgetConfigPanel.tsx | Adds context-aware sections (pivot/chart/table), breadcrumb logic, and I18nLabel normalization. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx | Routes object-bound table/pivot to async wrappers; clamps layout width; renders widget description. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/PivotTable.tsx | Adds friendly empty state and improves totals styling. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectPivotTable.tsx | New async wrapper to fetch object records and feed PivotTable. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectDataTable.tsx | New async wrapper to fetch object records and feed data-table, with auto-derived columns. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/MetricWidget.tsx | Adds overflow protection and truncation for metric cards. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/*.test.tsx | Updates/adds tests for routing, empty states, and config panel behavior. |
| ROADMAP.md | Documents Phase 13 completion for these enhancements. |
</details>

The pivot-specific config fields added here (`rowField`, `columnField`, `showRowTotals`, `showColumnTotals`, etc.) are stored on the widget draft as top-level keys, but `DashboardRenderer` builds pivot schemas purely from `widget.options` (plus `widget.object/filter`). This means edits made in these sections won’t be reflected in live preview/rendering unless you either (a) write these values into `widget.options` when saving/updating the draft, or (b) update `DashboardRenderer` to treat these as widget-level overrides (similar to `categoryField`/`valueField` for charts).

`normalizedConfig` coerces `title`/`description` I18nLabel objects into plain strings before passing them into `useConfigDraft`, and `onSave` persists the draft verbatim. This will drop the original `{ key, defaultValue }` structure (and translation key) on save whenever the user saves any change. If preserving i18n metadata matters, prefer keeping the original values in the draft and only resolving to a display string in the input renderer (or store both raw + display values).

`pivotValueField` is used as the config key for the pivot “Values → Field” selector, but the pivot renderer/schema expects `valueField` (matching `PivotTableSchema.valueField`). As-is, user selections will be written to `pivotValueField` and won’t affect the pivot output unless additional mapping is added. Consider renaming this field key to `valueField` (and migrating any saved configs if needed).
```suggestion
    ? buildFieldCombobox('valueField', 'Field', 'Select value field…', availableFields)
    : { key: 'valueField', label: 'Field', type: 'input', placeholder: 'e.g. amount' };
```

The new chart-specific fields (`xAxisLabel`, `yAxisLabel`, `showLegend`) are added to the widget draft, but `DashboardRenderer` doesn’t read these keys when constructing the `chart` / `object-chart` schemas. As a result, changes in this section won’t affect rendering unless these values are mapped into the rendered schema (or stored under `widget.options` and consumed from there).

This object-provider table path now honors `widget.searchable`/`widget.pagination`, but the non-object table fallback below still forces `searchable: false` / `pagination: false`. Given `WidgetConfigPanel` now exposes these toggles for table widgets, consider applying the same values in the non-object path (or deferring to `options.searchable`/`options.pagination`) so the toggles work consistently.

`WidgetConfigPanel` adds many pivot settings (row/column/value fields, totals toggles, sort settings, format) as widget-level draft keys, but this pivot routing passes through only `options` (and object binding) and doesn’t merge any widget-level overrides. Unless those settings are stored under `widget.options`, pivot edits from the config panel won’t affect the rendered `object-pivot`/`pivot` schema. Consider merging widget-level values into the returned pivot schema (similar to the chart path’s `categoryField`/`valueField` overrides) or updating the editor to write into `options`.

The empty-state SVG is purely decorative, but it doesn’t set `aria-hidden="true"` (or an accessible name). This can cause screen readers to announce it as an unlabelled graphic. Consider marking the SVG as decorative (`aria-hidden` + `focusable="false"`) or adding appropriate `role`/`aria-label`.
